core_meaning.short_meaning: Hardy enduring plant; companion Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man al-Ansari.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Qatadah (قَتَادَة) is an authentic Arabic masculine name meaning 'hardy, resilient plant' or 'symbol of enduring steadfastness'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man al-Ansari, a heroic companion present at Badr whose eye was struck at Uhud and miraculously healed by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: A single tree or stem of qatad (a resilient thorny desert shrub), representing patience, rugged strength, and endurance.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root q-t-d refers to the resilient desert plant celebrated in classical Arabic poetry for its perseverance in arid climates. As a personal name, Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man was an early convert from the Aws tribe who defended the Prophet ﷺ at the Battle of Uhud. During the battle, his eye was struck out of its socket; the Prophet ﷺ set it back in place with his hand and supplicated, whereupon it became his sharper and better eye.
